transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Mrs. Al-Rashid, thank you for seeing me. I need to tell you something important about your care.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Yes, doctor. I am listening.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I made a mistake. The machine that checks your heart, the ECG, showed a problem four hours ago. I did not look at that result right away. This meant we did not start your treatment as quickly as we should have.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: A mistake? By you?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Yes. I missed the alert from the machine. It was my responsibility to check it, and I did not. Do you understand what I mean so far?

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I do not know. I thought everything was... the machine says a problem, but you did not see?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Exactly. The machine flagged the heart problem, but I did not review it for four hours. That is why the diagnosis was late. Does that make sense?

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I am... I am very surprised. I thought you are the expert. Why did this happen?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I am very sorry, Mrs. Al-Rashid. I take full responsibility for this. I apologize for the delay in your care.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I feel very scared now. My heart is beating fast. I thought I was in safe hands.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: It is completely understandable that you feel scared and let down. You trusted us to keep you safe, and I failed to do that in this moment.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I cannot believe a doctor would—

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I know this is shocking. I can see how distressing this is for you to hear.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I just want to know if I am okay now. Is my heart—

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We have started the medicine now. We are monitoring you closely. But I want to be honest, the four-hour delay was a mistake.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Why did you not check? Were you not there?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I was in the building, but I did not check the screen for your specific result. It was my error.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I feel very small. I did not expect this from a doctor.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I hear how disappointing this is. You expected a high standard of care, and I did not meet it.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: What will happen now? Will I be okay?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I have a plan. First, we are keeping you on this monitor for the next twenty-four hours. Every hour, a nurse will check your levels and report directly to me.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: And if it happens again?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I have to go check on another patient quickly, but we will talk more about the long term. Right now, the next step is that I will see you again in one hour to check your progress.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: But I have more questions. You said you have to go?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I really do need to wrap this up for a moment. We can talk more later.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I feel very confused. You say you are sorry, but you are rushing away.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I understand that feels contradictory. I am truly sorry for the mistake, and I care about your recovery. I just need to step out for a few minutes.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I do not know what to think.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I will be back in one hour. Please tell the nurse if you feel any more pain. I will see you very soon.

H.justification: Resident uses rushing language multiple times at the end ('wrap this up', 'step out for a few minutes', 'need to go check on another patient quickly').

E.justification: Error named in first turn, lay language used, comprehension checked twice ('Do you understand what I mean so far?', 'Does that make sense?'), and no false reassurance given.

A.justification: Direct apologies used, resident takes full responsibility ('I take full responsibility', 'It was my error'), and maintains accountability despite patient pushback.

R.justification: Specific emotions named back at least twice ('scared and let down', 'shocking', 'distressing', 'disappointing') and engages with the patient's emotional bids.

T.justification: Provides specific next steps and timelines (monitoring for 24 hours, return in one hour), but fails to address prevention or name a specific patient role in the plan.
